question: Every year on 2nd October, the Prime Minister of India pays homage to Mahatma Gandhi at ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Raj Ghat.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi:-**

 
 
• **He is commonly known as Mahatma Gandhi, was born on October 2**, and every year on that day, a **celebration known as Gandhi Jayanti is held in his honour.**
 
• Mahatma Gandhi, who is revered as the **"Father of the Nation," **was one of the most important figures in **the Indian freedom struggle.**
 
• **In New Delhi's Raj Ghat, prayer vigils are held in front of Gandhi's statue as a mark of respect.**
 
• The **President and Prime Minister of India are present at Mahatma Gandhi's memorial to pay their respects.**
 
• To recognise his contribution to the nation, **October 2 is recognised as a national holiday.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India Gate**

 
 
• ​The **All-India Military** Memorial, formerly known as the **India Gate**, is a military memorial that can be found next to the Kartavya route on the eastern edge of New Delhi's "**ceremonial axis**," also known as the duty path.
 
• It serves as a memorial to the **84,000 British Indian Army **personnel who lost their lives between 1914 and 1921 while serving in the **Third Anglo-Afghan War**, in France, Flanders, Mesopotamia, Persia, East Africa, Gallipoli, and other locations in the Near and Far East.
 
 
 
• **Amar Jawan Jyoti**
 
 
• ​After the **Indo-Pakistani War of 1971,** an Indian memorial known as **Amar Jawan Jyoti **was conceptualized, built, and dedicated on January 26, 1972.
 
• Up until February 2019, when the new **National War Monument** and its own flame were erected and lighted, it served as India's national war monument.
 
 
 
• **Vijay Ghat**
 
 
• **​Lal Bahadur Shastri **was the second **Prime Minister of India,** and his memorial park is called **Vijay Ghat**, which translates to "**Victory Bank.**" Its location next to a man-made lake gives the area a pleasant atmosphere, and the well-kept landscaped gardens, lawns, and trees around the area contribute to preserving the tranquilly of the place.
 
 

5f:T
